I read the whole file. I also read the downstream uses of `equalizerMapOfCommuting` in Scheme/EquivalenceRelationRankEqualizer.lean (lines 60–158).

The only simp-relevant declaration is `coe_equalizerMapOfCommuting`. It is `@[simp]`, proved by `rfl`, and has a sensible orientation: the left side is the subtype coercion of the mapped element, and the right side is `f x.1`, which is simpler. The left side has the shape simp needs, so I see no risk of a loop or of competing rules.

The localization proof in this file does not call that simp lemma. It uses `change` and `Subtype.ext_iff` instead. The downstream file also only passes the map to `equalizerMapOfCommuting_isLocalizationAway`. I found no use that would gain from an extra simp lemma, so I did not recommend one.

`algebraMap_eq_iff_mul_eq_of_isIdempotentElem` is an iff with hypotheses, and its right side adds a multiplication by `e`. Making it simp would risk unwanted expansion, so leaving it unannotated looks right. The `simp` and `simpa` calls in the proofs use explicit lemma lists.

I did not run Lean, so I cannot rule out cases where simp fails or is slow.
